speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to narrow this down, have the pain worsened after specific activities like climbing stairs or twisting? Have you noticed any locking, clicking, or instability when moving the knee?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (Oligoarticular) or Sickle Cell Disease (Avascular Necrosis). Given the patient's age (18 months) and the onset of swelling after minor activity without trauma, I need to differentiate between inflammatory causes and hemoglobinopathies. Please describe the appearance of the swelling: is it red, warm to the touch, and does the child have any other symptoms like fever or fatigue?
